liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (3 reviews): Described as the definitive, extremely tight version, with Pigpen leading the band through a cosmic, harmonically perfect jam; Reviewer asks how often Easy Wind was played after this night in 1971 [10][13][14]
- **Smokestack Lightning** (2 reviews): Smokestack is singled out as nice, and the third disc is said to flow well; Smokestack, along with Easy Wind, is called at its finest [7][15]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): The audience goes wild during this song on the audience recording [12]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Deal [19]

## The recordings

- **gd71-02-19.sbd.orf.1029.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [1]. Said about its sound: This copy is less degraded than the run's other nights and is very clean, showing the Betty Boards' quality; Mono recording; slight whine reduced with a notch filter [1][8]
- **gd71-02-19.matrix.chappell.31210.sbeok.flacf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 159 min; rated 4.27/5 by 11 [2]. Said about its sound: Matrix is a clear, crisp upgrade over the audience tape, with vocals and instruments mixed with the lively crowd [17]
- **gd1971-02-19.aud.Vadnais.30230.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 134 min; rated 3.56/5 by 9 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is better than average thanks to modern technical help, with the flavor of the Dead; most people have this run from soundboards; Audience recording is of modest quality but captures crowd reactions, which are loud during I Know You Rider [11][12]
- **gd1971-02-19.132102.flac16**: audience recording; 6 songs; 38 min [5]

## Around the show

- Some garage-band moments appear, but overall the band plays as though they were recording it [9]
- Crowd sounds small, perhaps 200 people, and the tape opens with band tuning and snatches of melodies before Truckin' [17]
- Show also featured NRPS; part of it was officially released as Three From The Vault in 2007 [3]
- NRPS also appeared on the bill; show was officially released as Three From The Vault in 2007 [5]
- Reviewer prefers the 2/18 and 2/24 shows over this one within the run [7]
- 2/18, the run's first night, is the most acclaimed, with its setlist and being the last show with Mickey [8]
- Reviewer says this period through late August 1971 was the last of the heavier concerts [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-02-19.sbd.orf.1029.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: One of the first tapes the reviewer's trading contact Dr. Flashback traded for in the 1980s; first show collected from this run; Seven-inch two-track reel with Dolby A at 7.5 ips, transferred via PCM501ES and Fostex D5, then Cool Edit Pro filtering, to SHN [1][9]
- **gd71-02-19.matrix.chappell.31210.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Clinton Vadnais and Chris Chappell; source: Matrix [2]
- **gd1971-02-19.aud.Vadnais.30230.flac16**: transferred by Clinton Vadnais; source: Audience [4]
- **gd1971-02-19.132102.flac16**: source: Partial 1st Set; it is supposidly 4th gen audience recording from an unknown source; the transfer was not documented [5]. Also: Partial audience recording, possibly made by a venue worker with microphones in the balcony [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by crepuscularthad.blogspot.com: [Brokedown Palace: The Capitol Theatre and the Grateful Dead](https://crepuscularthad.blogspot.com/2017/03/capitol-theatre-and-grateful-dead.html) [20]
